number.why: HR 0.80 (0.71-0.91) is major bleeding for HIGH-dose edoxaban vs warfarin in the three-arm ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48. It is not the low-dose 0.47 in the same sentence. The registry confirms it in the safety set, on treatment.

quotes.span: The annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.43% with warfarin versus 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001).
groups High Dose Edoxaban/Placebo Warfarin, Warfarin/Placebo Edoxaban | Cox Proportional Hazard .80 (95% CI .707 to .914)

entry.why: Adults 21 or older with documented AF. Moderate/severe mitral stenosis and mechanical valves are excluded, which makes the population non-valvular AF.

quotes.span: 21 years of age or older; male or female.
History of documented AF within the prior 12 months
Subjects with moderate or severe mitral stenosis, unresected atrial myxoma, or a mechanical heart valve

missed: The served analysis_set label 'intention-to-treat' is contradicted by the registry (safety set, on treatment); the ruling records this. If the review ever serves the low-dose arm too, the shared warfarin arm would need splitting. As served, one arm is used and there is no double count.
